title: Plus-que-parfait
bridge: In Spanish we use the past perfect to talk about something that happened BEFORE another past event: 'Cuando llegué, ya habían comido.' French works exactly the same with the plus-que-parfait: it is the 'past of the past.' The key difference is that in French, the agreement of the participle with être is obligatory and visible.
rule:
Formation: auxiliary (avoir or être) in IMPARFAIT + past participle.

• Verbs with AVOIR (majority): j'avais parlé, tu avais fini, il avait pris, nous avions vu, vous aviez fait, ils avaient dit.
• Verbs with ÊTRE (movement and reflexive): j'étais allé(e), tu étais parti(e), il était venu, elle était venue, nous étions arrivé(e)s, vous étiez sorti(e)(s), ils étaient tombés, elles étaient tombées.

Main uses:
1. Past of the past: action occurring BEFORE another past action (with passé composé or imparfait).
   → 'Quand il est arrivé, nous avions déjà mangé.'
2. With 'si' in type 3 conditional: 'Si j'avais su, je serais venu.'
3. With 'après que': 'Après qu'elle eut fini...' (formal, rare).

Common irregular participles: être→été, avoir→eu, faire→fait, prendre→pris, venir→venu, partir→parti, voir→vu, dire→dit, écrire→écrit, mettre→mis, naître→né, mourir→mort.

concept_examples.text: Il avait déjà mangé quand je suis arrivé.
concept_examples.translation: He had already eaten when I arrived.
concept_examples.phonetic: /i‿l‿a.vɛ de.ʒa mɑ̃.ʒe kɑ̃ ʒə sɥi‿z‿a.ʁi.ve/

concept_examples.text: Elle était partie avant que tu appelles.
concept_examples.translation: She had already left before you called.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɛ.l‿e.tɛ paʁ.ti a.vɑ̃ kə ty a.pɛl/

concept_examples.text: Nous avions étudié toute la nuit.
concept_examples.translation: We had studied all night.
concept_examples.phonetic: /nu‿z‿a.vjɔ̃ e.ty.dje tut la nɥi/

common_error.wrong: Quand je suis arrivé, il a déjà mangé.
common_error.correct: Quand je suis arrivé, il avait déjà mangé.
common_error.explanation: In Spanish we sometimes tolerate the present perfect in contexts where anteriority is implied, but in French the temporal sequence must be marked with the plus-que-parfait. The passé composé (a mangé) does not express that the action was prior to another past action; that role belongs exclusively to the plus-que-parfait (avait mangé).

examples.original: J'avais oublié mes clés.
examples.translation: I had forgotten my keys.
examples.note: Avoir in imparfait (avais) + participle (oublié). Basic structure.

examples.original: Tu avais fini tes devoirs ?
examples.translation: Had you finished your homework?
examples.note: Direct question with plus-que-parfait. In informal speech, the intonation rises at the end.

examples.original: Ils étaient déjà partis.
examples.translation: They had already left.
examples.note: Être + participle: partis agrees in masculine plural. Compare: elles étaient parties.

examples.original: Quand nous sommes arrivés, le film avait déjà commencé.
examples.phonetic: /kɑ̃ nu sɔm‿z‿a.ʁi.ve lə film a.vɛ de.ʒa kɔ.mɑ̃.se/
examples.translation: When we arrived, the movie had already started.
examples.note: Main clause in passé composé + subordinate with plus-que-parfait: the temporal sequence is clear.

examples.original: Elle n'avait jamais visité Paris avant ce voyage.
examples.phonetic: /ɛl na.vɛ ʒa.mɛ vi.zi.te pa.ʁi a.vɑ̃ sə vwa.jaʒ/
examples.translation: She had never visited Paris before that trip.
examples.note: Negation ne...jamais with plus-que-parfait. Very common to express prior experiences.

examples.original: Il a reconnu la chanson qu'il avait entendue enfant.
examples.translation: He recognized the song he had heard as a child.
examples.note: Agreement of the participle: entendue agrees with 'chanson' (feminine singular), antecedent of the relative qu'.

examples.original: Si j'avais su, je ne serais pas venu.
examples.phonetic: /si ʒa.vɛ sy ʒə nə sə.ʁɛ pa vəny/
examples.translation: If I had known, I would not have come.
examples.note: Si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé. It is the equivalent of the Spanish 'si hubiera + habría'. Never 'si j'aurais su'.

examples.original: Si tu avais étudié, tu aurais réussi l'examen.
examples.phonetic: /si ty a.vɛ‿z‿e.ty.dje ty o.ʁɛ ʁe.y.si lek.sa.mɛ̃/
examples.translation: If you had studied, you would have passed the exam.
examples.note: Complete type 3 structure. The si clause takes plus-que-parfait, the main clause takes conditionnel passé.

examples.original: Elle aurait pu venir si elle n'avait pas eu de réunion.
examples.phonetic: /ɛ‿l‿o.ʁɛ py və.niʁ si ɛl na.vɛ pa‿z‿y də ʁe.y.njɔ̃/
examples.translation: She could have come if she had not had a meeting.
examples.note: Inverted order: main clause (conditionnel passé) before the si clause (plus-que-parfait).

examples.original: Je regrettais de ne pas avoir dit la vérité avant qu'il soit parti.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə ʁə.ɡʁɛ.tɛ də nə pa‿z‿a.vwaʁ di la ve.ʁi.te a.vɑ̃ ki‿l‿swa paʁ.ti/
examples.translation: I regretted not having told the truth before he left.
examples.note: Literary/formal use: anteriority expressed with compound infinitive (avoir dit) instead of plus-que-parfait.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pourquoi tu n'es pas venu à la fête hier soir ?
dialogue.translation: Why didn't you come to the party last night?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: J'avais complètement oublié ! J'avais noté la date, mais j'avais perdu mon agenda.
dialogue.translation: I had completely forgotten! I had noted the date, but I had lost my planner.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Dommage. On avait préparé un gâteau pour ton anniversaire.
dialogue.translation: Too bad. We had prepared a cake for your birthday.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Si j'avais su, je serais certainement venu !
dialogue.translation: If I had known, I would certainly have come!

title: Conditionnel présent
bridge: The French present conditional is equivalent to the Spanish 'haría / comería / vendría'. It is used for hypotheses (si + imparfait → conditionnel), polite requests, and dreams. The good news: the stem is identical to the futur simple, only the endings change (which are those of the imparfait: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient).
rule:
Formation: STEM of the futur simple + endings of the imparfait.

Endings: -ais / -ais / -ait / -ions / -iez / -aient

REGULAR STEMS:
• -er verbs: full infinitive → parler → je parlerais, tu parlerais, il parlerait, nous parlerions, vous parleriez, ils parleraient.
• -ir verbs: full infinitive → finir → je finirais, tu finirais, il finirait, nous finirions, vous finiriez, ils finiraient.
• -re verbs: drop the final -e → prendre → je prendrais.

IRREGULAR STEMS (same as in futur simple):
• être → ser- : je serais
• avoir → aur- : j'aurais
• aller → ir- : j'irais
• faire → fer- : je ferais
• pouvoir → pourr- : je pourrais
• vouloir → voudr- : je voudrais
• venir → viendr- : je viendrais
• savoir → saur- : je saurais
• voir → verr- : je verrais
• devoir → devr- : je devrais
• recevoir → recevr- : je recevrais
• envoyer → enverr- : j'enverrais
• courir → courr- : je courrais
• tenir → tiendr- : je tiendrais

USES:
1. Hypothesis (type 2 conditional): si + imparfait → conditionnel présent.
   → 'Si j'avais de l'argent, j'achèterais une maison.'
2. Politeness (softened requests): 'Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.'
3. Dreams and wishes: 'J'aimerais vivre à Paris.'
4. Unconfirmed information (journalistic style): 'Le président serait malade.'
5. Advice: 'Tu devrais aller chez le médecin.'

concept_examples.text: Si j'avais le temps, je voyagerais partout.
concept_examples.translation: If I had time, I would travel everywhere.
concept_examples.phonetic: /si ʒa.vɛ lə tɑ̃ ʒə vwa.ja.ʒ‿ʁɛ paʁ.tu/

concept_examples.text: Je voudrais réserver une table pour deux personnes.
concept_examples.translation: I would like to book a table for two people.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə vu.dʁɛ ʁe.zɛʁ.ve yn ta.blə puʁ dø pɛʁ.sɔn/

concept_examples.text: Tu devrais arrêter de fumer.
concept_examples.translation: You should stop smoking.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ty də.vʁɛ a.ʁɛ.te də fy.me/

common_error.wrong: Si j'aurais de l'argent, j'achèterais une maison.
common_error.correct: Si j'avais de l'argent, j'achèterais une maison.
common_error.explanation: In French, the 'si' clause for type 2 hypotheses NEVER takes the conditional: always use the imparfait. The conditional goes only in the main clause. 'Si j'aurais...' is the most frequent error among Spanish speakers because in Spanish 'si tuviera / si tendría' can alternate colloquially, but in French the rule is strict: si + imparfait → conditionnel.

examples.original: Je voudrais un verre d'eau, s'il vous plaît.
examples.translation: I would like a glass of water, please.
examples.note: Vouloir in the conditional (voudrais) is the most polite way to ask for something. Much more polite than 'je veux'.

examples.original: Vous pourriez m'aider, s'il vous plaît ?
examples.translation: Could you help me, please?
examples.note: Pouvoir in the conditional (pourriez) for formal requests. The rising intonation marks the question.

examples.original: J'aimerais apprendre la guitare.
examples.translation: I would like to learn the guitar.
examples.note: Aimer in the conditional expresses a personal desire. Equivalent to the Spanish 'me gustaría / me encantaría'.

examples.original: Si je parlais français couramment, je chercherais un emploi à Paris.
examples.phonetic: /si ʒə paʁ.lɛ fʁɑ̃.sɛ ku.ʁa.mɑ̃ ʒə ʃɛʁ.ʃ‿ʁɛ‿œ̃‿ɑ̃.plwa a pa.ʁi/
examples.translation: If I spoke French fluently, I would look for a job in Paris.
examples.note: Si + imparfait (parlais) → conditionnel (chercherais). Hypothesis that the speaker considers unlikely or unreal in the present.

examples.original: Qu'est-ce que tu ferais si tu gagnais à la loterie ?
examples.phonetic: /kɛs kə ty fə.ʁɛ si ty ɡa.ɲɛ a la lɔ.tʁi/
examples.translation: What would you do if you won the lottery?
examples.note: Classic question with type 2 hypothesis. Ferais (faire) and gagnais (gagner) show regular and irregular forms.

examples.original: Si elle avait une voiture, elle pourrait venir nous voir plus souvent.
examples.phonetic: /si ɛ‿l‿a.vɛ yn vwa.tyʁ ɛl pu.ʁɛ və.niʁ nu vwaʁ ply su.vɑ̃/
examples.translation: If she had a car, she could come see us more often.
examples.note: Pouvoir (pourrait) in the present conditional. Avoir (avait) in the si clause.

examples.original: On vivrait mieux si on travaillait moins.
examples.translation: We would live better if we worked less.
examples.note: On as an impersonal/informal subject equivalent to 'we'. Vivre has an irregular stem: vivr-.

examples.original: Tu devrais parler à ton patron de cette situation.
examples.phonetic: /ty də.vʁɛ paʁ.le a tɔ̃ pa.tʁɔ̃ də sɛt si.tɥa.sjɔ̃/
examples.translation: You should talk to your boss about this situation.
examples.note: Devoir in the conditional (devrais) to give advice in a softened way. More polite than the imperative.

examples.original: À ta place, je ne dirais rien.
examples.phonetic: /a ta plas ʒə nə di.ʁɛ ʁjɛ̃/
examples.translation: In your place, I wouldn't say anything.
examples.note: 'À ta place' (in your place) + conditional is a very common formula for giving indirect advice.

examples.original: Selon les médias, le gouvernement serait prêt à négocier.
examples.phonetic: /sə.lɔ̃ le me.dja lə ɡu.vɛʁ.nə.mɑ̃ sə.ʁɛ pʁɛ a ne.ɡɔ.sje/
examples.translation: According to the media, the government would be ready to negotiate.
examples.note: Journalistic use: the conditional marks unconfirmed information or rumor. Equivalent to the Spanish 'estaría / habría'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Qu'est-ce que tu ferais si tu pouvais habiter n'importe où dans le monde ?
dialogue.translation: What would you do if you could live anywhere in the world?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Je choisirais le Japon ! J'aimerais apprendre la langue et découvrir la culture.
dialogue.translation: I would choose Japan! I would like to learn the language and discover the culture.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Et moi, je voudrais vivre près de la mer. Je me lèverais tôt chaque matin pour me baigner.
dialogue.translation: And I would like to live near the sea. I would get up early every morning to swim.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Tu devrais chercher un travail dans une ville côtière, alors !
dialogue.translation: Then you should look for a job in a coastal city!

title: Conditionnel passé
bridge: The French past conditional is equivalent to the Spanish 'habría hecho / habría venido'. It is formed with avoir or être in the conditionnel présent + past participle. Its most characteristic use at B1 level is REPROACH and LAMENT: 'Tu aurais dû...' (You should have...) and 'J'aurais aimé...' (I would have liked...). It also completes the third conditional (si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé).
rule:
Formation: auxiliary (avoir or être) in the CONDITIONNEL PRÉSENT + past participle.

With AVOIR:
• j'aurais parlé / tu aurais fini / il aurait pris
• nous aurions vu / vous auriez fait / ils auraient dit

With ÊTRE (verbs of movement + reflexive verbs):
• je serais allé(e) / tu serais parti(e) / il serait venu
• elle serait venue / nous serions arrivé(e)s / vous seriez sorti(e)(s)
• ils seraient tombés / elles seraient tombées

AGREEMENT with être: the past participle agrees in gender and number with the subject.
AGREEMENT with avoir: the past participle agrees with the direct object if it is placed before the verb.

MAIN USES:
1. Third conditional (unreal past hypothesis): main clause.
   → 'Si j'avais su, je serais venu.'
2. Reproach (someone did or did not do something): 'Tu aurais dû le dire!' (You should have said it!)
3. Personal lament: 'J'aurais voulu être là.' (I would have wanted to be there.)
4. Unconfirmed information in the past (press): 'Le ministre aurait démissionné.'

MOST USED REPROACH FORMULAS:
• Tu aurais dû + infinitive (You should have...)
• Tu n'aurais pas dû + infinitive (You should not have...)
• Il aurait fallu + infinitive (It would have been necessary to...)
• J'aurais pu + infinitive (I could have...)

concept_examples.text: Si j'avais su, je n'aurais jamais accepté.
concept_examples.translation: If I had known, I would never have accepted.
concept_examples.phonetic: /si ʒa.vɛ sy ʒə no.ʁɛ ʒa.mɛ ak.sɛp.te/

concept_examples.text: Tu aurais dû m'appeler avant de partir.
concept_examples.translation: You should have called me before leaving.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ty o.ʁɛ dy ma.p.le a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ/

concept_examples.text: Elle serait arrivée plus tôt si elle avait pris le train.
concept_examples.translation: She would have arrived earlier if she had taken the train.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɛl sə.ʁɛ‿t‿a.ʁi.ve ply to si ɛ‿l‿a.vɛ pʁi lə tʁɛ̃/

common_error.wrong: Tu aurais dû de le dire.
common_error.explanation: After 'devoir' (dû) and modal verbs in general, the infinitive goes DIRECTLY without a preposition. The preposition 'de' is not used between the modal auxiliary and the infinitive. In Spanish we colloquially say 'deberías de haberlo dicho' with 'de', but in French that particle does not exist in this construction.

examples.original: J'aurais voulu être médecin.
examples.translation: I would have liked to be a doctor.
examples.note: Vouloir (aurais voulu) expresses a desire that was not fulfilled in the past. Very common in conversation.

examples.original: On aurait pu rester plus longtemps.
examples.translation: We could have stayed longer.
examples.note: Pouvoir (aurait pu) expresses a past possibility not taken advantage of. On = we (informal).

examples.original: J'aurais aimé te voir avant ton départ.
examples.translation: I would have liked to see you before your departure.
examples.note: Aimer in the past conditional to express polite regret. Softer and more empathetic tone than 'je regrette'.

examples.original: Tu aurais dû prévenir tout le monde !
examples.phonetic: /ty o.ʁɛ dy pʁe.və.niʁ tu lə mɔ̃d/
examples.translation: You should have warned everyone!
examples.note: Devoir (aurais dû) + infinitive = reproach for something that was not done. The exclamation intensifies the reproach.

examples.original: Vous n'auriez pas dû lire cette lettre, elle était privée.
examples.phonetic: /vu no.ʁje pa dy liʁ sɛt lɛtʁ ɛ‿l‿e.tɛ pʁi.ve/
examples.translation: You should not have read that letter, it was private.
examples.note: Ne pas devoir in the past conditional = reproach for something that WAS done but should not have been. Formal form with vous.

examples.original: Il aurait fallu vérifier les informations avant de publier.
examples.phonetic: /i‿l‿o.ʁɛ fa.ly ve.ʁi.fje le‿z‿ɛ̃.fɔʁ.ma.sjɔ̃ a.vɑ̃ də py.blje/
examples.translation: It would have been necessary to verify the information before publishing.
examples.note: Falloir (aurait fallu) impersonal is more neutral than devoir: it criticizes a situation without directly blaming someone.

examples.original: Elle aurait pu nous avertir plus tôt !
examples.translation: She could have warned us earlier!
examples.note: Pouvoir (aurait pu) as reproach: points out a possibility that existed but was not taken advantage of.

examples.original: Si nous avions pris l'autre route, nous serions arrivés à l'heure.
examples.phonetic: /si nu‿z‿a.vjɔ̃ pʁi lo.tʁ ʁut nu sə.ʁjɔ̃‿z‿a.ʁi.ve a lœʁ/
examples.translation: If we had taken the other route, we would have arrived on time.
examples.note: Plus-que-parfait (avions pris) + conditionnel passé with être (serions arrivés). Agreement: arrivés in masculine plural.

examples.original: Si tu avais dormi suffisamment, tu n'aurais pas fait cette erreur.
examples.phonetic: /si ty a.vɛ dɔʁ.mi sy.fi.za.mɑ̃ ty no.ʁɛ pa fɛ sɛ‿t‿ɛ.ʁœʁ/
examples.translation: If you had slept enough, you would not have made that mistake.
examples.note: It has both a reproach function and a third conditional at the same time. Very natural in everyday conversation.

examples.original: Selon les enquêteurs, l'accident aurait pu être évité.
examples.phonetic: /sə.lɔ̃ le‿z‿ɑ̃.kɛ.tœʁ lak.si.dɑ̃ o.ʁɛ py ɛtʁ e.vi.te/
examples.translation: According to the investigators, the accident could have been avoided.
examples.note: Journalistic/legal use of the conditionnel passé for unconfirmed information. Pouvoir (aurait pu) + passive infinitive.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu sais que Léa n'est pas venue à la réunion hier ?
dialogue.translation: Do you know that Léa didn't come to the meeting yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, elle aurait dû prévenir au moins ! On l'a attendue pendant une heure.
dialogue.translation: Yes, she should have at least warned us! We waited for her for an hour.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Si elle nous avait envoyé un message, on aurait pu commencer sans elle.
dialogue.translation: If she had sent us a message, we could have started without her.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exactement. Il aurait fallu mieux organiser tout ça.
dialogue.translation: Exactly. It would have been necessary to organize all this better.

title: La voix passive
bridge: The passive voice in French works the same as in Spanish: 'El libro fue escrito por ella' → 'Le livre a été écrit par elle'. The formula is être + past participle agreeing + par (by). The important difference: in French, 'on' (impersonal active) is used a lot as an alternative to the passive, something we don't do in Spanish with the same frequency. Also: the participle ALWAYS agrees with the subject, like an adjective.
rule:
FORMATION:
Subject + être (conjugated) + agreeing participle + par + agent.

Most used tenses:
• Présent: Le gâteau est mangé par les enfants.
• Passé composé: Le gâteau a été mangé par les enfants.
• Imparfait: Le gâteau était mangé par les enfants chaque dimanche.
• Futur simple: Le gâteau sera mangé par les enfants.
• Conditionnel: Le gâteau serait mangé si...
• Plus-que-parfait: Le gâteau avait été mangé avant notre arrivée.

PARTICIPLE AGREEMENT (mandatory):
• Masculine singular subject: Le document est signé.
• Feminine singular subject: La lettre est signée.
• Masculine plural subject: Les documents sont signés.
• Feminine plural subject: Les lettres sont signées.

PAR vs. DE:
• par: active agent, concrete action: 'Le livre a été écrit par Camus.'
• de: resulting state, more permanent or psychological situation: 'Il est aimé de tous.' (more literary/formal)

WHEN TO USE THE PASSIVE vs. ON:
Passive: 'Le voleur a été arrêté par la police.'
Active with ON: 'On a arrêté le voleur.' (more frequent in spoken language)
Practical rule: in conversation, 'on + active' is preferred. The passive is more frequent in written texts, journalism, formal language.

VERBS THAT DO NOT ALLOW THE PASSIVE: intransitive verbs (aller, venir, partir...) and verbs with an indirect object (parler à, téléphoner à, obéir à...) cannot be turned into the passive voice.

concept_examples.text: Ce roman a été écrit par une jeune autrice française.
concept_examples.translation: This novel was written by a young French female author.
concept_examples.phonetic: /sə ʁɔ.mɑ̃ a e.te e.kʁi paʁ yn ʒœ̃ o.tʁis fʁɑ̃.sɛz/

concept_examples.text: Les résultats seront annoncés demain.
concept_examples.translation: The results will be announced tomorrow.
concept_examples.phonetic: /le ʁe.zyl.ta sə.ʁɔ̃ a.nɔ̃.se də.mɛ̃/

concept_examples.text: On a construit ce pont en 1889.
concept_examples.translation: This bridge was built in 1889. (lit.: They built this bridge in 1889.)
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ a kɔ̃s.tʁɥi sə pɔ̃ ɑ̃ mil‿ɥi‿t‿sɑ̃kat.vɛ̃.nœf/
concept_examples.note: Active alternative with 'on' — preferred in informal speech

common_error.wrong: La lettre est écrit par Marie.
common_error.correct: La lettre est écrite par Marie.
common_error.explanation: The past participle in the passive voice agrees in gender and number with the subject, exactly like an adjective. 'Lettre' is feminine singular, therefore the participle must be 'écrite' (not 'écrit'). This is the most frequent error: forgetting the agreement. To avoid it, always ask yourself 'what is the gender and number of the subject?' and adjust the participle.

examples.original: Le repas est préparé par ma mère.
examples.phonetic: /lə ʁə.pa ɛ pʁe.pa.ʁe paʁ ma mɛʁ/
examples.translation: The meal is prepared by my mother.
examples.note: Basic present passive. Repas (masculine singular) → préparé without additional marking.

examples.original: La porte est fermée à clé.
examples.translation: The door is locked.
examples.note: Porte (feminine singular) → fermée with -e. Without agent: it is unknown or doesn't matter who closed it.

examples.original: Les fenêtres sont ouvertes par le vent.
examples.translation: The windows are opened by the wind.
examples.note: Fenêtres (feminine plural) → ouvertes with -es. Ouvrir has an irregular participle: ouvert/ouverte/ouverts/ouvertes.

examples.original: Le suspect a été arrêté par les policiers hier soir.
examples.phonetic: /lə sys.pɛ a e.te a.ʁɛ.te paʁ le pɔ.li.sje jɛʁ swaʁ/
examples.translation: The suspect was arrested by the police officers last night.
examples.note: Passé composé passive: a été + participle. Arrêté agrees with suspect (m. sg.) → no marking.

examples.original: Ces photos ont été prises par un photographe professionnel.
examples.phonetic: /se fo.to ɔ̃ e.te pʁiz paʁ‿œ̃ fo.to.ɡʁaf pʁo.fɛ.sjɔ.nɛl/
examples.translation: These photos were taken by a professional photographer.
examples.note: Photos (feminine plural) → prises (irregular participle of prendre: pris → prises). Agreement visible in writing.

examples.original: Les résultats seront publiés la semaine prochaine.
examples.phonetic: /le ʁe.zyl.ta sə.ʁɔ̃ py.blje la s.mɛn pʁɔ.ʃɛn/
examples.translation: The results will be published next week.
examples.note: Future passive: seront + participle. Without agent: it is not known or doesn't matter who will publish.

examples.original: La décision avait été prise avant mon arrivée.
examples.phonetic: /la de.si.zjɔ̃ a.vɛ e.te pʁiz a.vɑ̃ mɔ̃‿n‿a.ʁi.ve/
examples.translation: The decision had been made before my arrival.
examples.note: Plus-que-parfait passive: avait été + participle. Décision (f. sg.) → prise.

examples.original: Les données personnelles sont collectées et analysées par les entreprises.
examples.phonetic: /le dɔ.ne pɛʁ.sɔ.nɛl sɔ̃ kɔ.lɛk.te e a.na.li.ze paʁ le‿z‿ɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz/
examples.translation: Companies collect and analyze personal data.
examples.note: Formal/journalistic register. Two coordinated participles: collectées and analysées, both f. pl.

examples.original: On collecte et on analyse les données personnelles dans ces entreprises.
examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ kɔ.lɛkt e ɔ̃‿n‿a.na.liz le dɔ.ne pɛʁ.sɔ.nɛl dɑ̃ se‿z‿ɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz/
examples.translation: In these companies, personal data is collected and analyzed.
examples.note: Same information with active 'on'. More natural in conversation. Both sentences are correct.

examples.original: Il est respecté de tous ses collègues.
examples.translation: He is respected by all his colleagues.
examples.note: De instead of par: permanent psychological/relational state. More literary. Compare: 'Il a été respecté par le jury' (concrete action) with par.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu as vu ? Le vieux musée a été rénové par la mairie.
dialogue.translation: Did you see? The old museum was renovated by the city hall.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui ! Et de nouvelles œuvres ont été achetées par la ville aussi.
dialogue.translation: Yes! And new works were also bought by the city.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: On dit que l'inauguration sera organisée le mois prochain.
dialogue.translation: They say the inauguration will be organized next month.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Super. J'espère que tout le monde sera invité, pas seulement les VIP !
dialogue.translation: Great. I hope everyone will be invited, not just the VIPs!

title: Le discours rapporté / Indirect speech
bridge: In Spanish, to go from direct to indirect speech, we change pronouns, verb tenses, and adverbs of place and time (e.g., 'dijo: «voy»' → 'dijo que iba'). In French, something very similar happens, but there are key differences: the tense changes are more rigid (the imperfect is maintained, the passé composé becomes plus-que-parfait), and the most common reporting verbs are 'dire', 'demander', and 'répondre'. Also, in French the conjunction 'que' is obligatory, just like in Spanish, but the phenomenon of 'queísmo' does not occur, nor is 'de' added as in Spanish ('dijo **de** que' is incorrect).
rule: To transform a sentence from direct to indirect speech in French, follow these steps: 1) Introduce the reporting verb (dire, demander, répondre, affirmer, etc.) followed by 'que' for statements or 'si' for yes/no questions, and by inversion or 'si' for questions with an interrogative word. 2) Adjust personal and possessive pronouns according to the new context. 3) Change the verb tenses applying tense concordance: - Présent → Imparfait (e.g., 'Il dit: «je veux»' → 'Il disait qu'il voulait'). - Passé composé → Plus-que-parfait (e.g., 'Il dit: «j'ai vu' → 'Il a dit qu'il avait vu'). - Futur simple → Conditionnel présent (e.g., 'Il dit: «je viendrai»' → 'Il a dit qu'il viendrait'). - The imparfait and plus-que-parfait do not change. 4) Adapt adverbs and expressions of time and place: 'aujourd'hui' → 'ce jour-là', 'demain' → 'le lendemain', 'hier' → 'la veille', 'ici' → 'là', 'maintenant' → 'alors'. Remember that in French, 'decir de que' is not used, but 'dire que'. For indirect questions, use 'demander si' for yes/no and 'demander où, quand, pourquoi, etc.' for questions with interrogatives, without inversion.

concept_examples.text: Il dit : « Je suis fatigué. »
concept_examples.translation: He says: 'I am tired.'
concept_examples.phonetic: /il di ʒə sɥi fatige/

concept_examples.text: Il dit qu'il est fatigué.
concept_examples.translation: He says that he is tired.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il di kil ɛ fatige/

concept_examples.text: Elle a dit : « J'ai vu un film. »
concept_examples.translation: She said: 'I saw a movie.'
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɛl a di ʒɛ vy œ̃ film/

concept_examples.text: Elle a dit qu'elle avait vu un film.
concept_examples.translation: She said that she had seen a movie.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɛl a di kɛl avɛ vy œ̃ film/

common_error.wrong: Il a dit qu'il a vu un film.
common_error.correct: Il a dit qu'il avait vu un film.
common_error.correct_alt: Il disait qu'il avait vu un film.
common_error.explanation: The error occurs because in Spanish, we often keep the present perfect or past simple in indirect speech (dijo que ha visto / dijo que vio). In French, tense concordance requires that the passé composé ('a vu') becomes plus-que-parfait ('avait vu') when the main verb is in a past tense. To avoid this, identify the tense of the reporting verb: if it is past, you must step back one step on the timeline.

examples.original: Il dit : « J'aime le chocolat. »
examples.translation: He says: 'I like chocolate.'
examples.note: Learn to introduce with 'que' and adjust the pronoun: 'J'aime' → 'qu'il aime'.

examples.original: Elle a dit : « Je suis contente. »
examples.translation: She said: 'I am happy.'
examples.note: Note that 'suis' (présent) becomes 'était' (imparfait) in indirect speech.

examples.original: Il répond : « Je viendrai demain. »
examples.translation: He replies: 'I will come tomorrow.'
examples.note: Futur simple 'viendrai' → conditionnel présent 'viendrait' in indirect speech.

examples.original: Il demande : « Est-ce que tu viens ? »
examples.translation: He asks: 'Are you coming?'
examples.note: For yes/no questions, use 'si' instead of 'que': 'Il demande si tu viens'.

examples.original: Elle demande : « Où habites-tu ? »
examples.translation: She asks: 'Where do you live?'
examples.note: Questions with an interrogative word keep the interrogative and use the normal form without inversion: 'Elle demande où tu habites'.

examples.original: Il demande : « Pourquoi êtes-vous en retard ? »
examples.phonetic: /il dəmɑ̃d purkwa ɛt vu ɑ̃ rətar/
examples.translation: He asks: 'Why are you late?'
examples.note: Pay attention to the pronoun change and word order: 'Il demande pourquoi vous êtes en retard'.

levels.label: Changements de temps et de contexte

examples.original: Hier, il m'a dit : « Je partirai demain. »
examples.phonetic: /jɛʁ il ma di ʒə partiʁe dəmɛ̃/
examples.translation: Yesterday he told me: 'I will leave tomorrow.'
examples.note: Practice the change from 'demain' to 'le lendemain' and from future to conditional: 'Il m'a dit qu'il partirait le lendemain'.

examples.original: Il disait : « Je travaillais ici. »
examples.translation: He was saying: 'I worked here.'
examples.note: The imparfait does not change: 'Il disait qu'il travaillait ici'.

examples.original: Elle a annoncé : « J'ai fini mes études. »
examples.phonetic: /ɛl a anɔ̃se ʒɛ fini mez etyd/
examples.translation: She announced: 'I have finished my studies.'
examples.note: Passé composé 'ai fini' → plus-que-parfait 'avait fini' in indirect speech.

title: Le gérondif et l'infinitif comme sujet et objet / The gerund and infinitive as subject and object
bridge: In Spanish, the infinitive can function as a subject ('swimming is good') and also as an object after a preposition ('I think about leaving'). In French, the infinitive fulfills the same functions, but with key differences: the French gerund (gérondif) is formed with 'en + present participle' and is only used for simultaneous actions or manner, never as a subject. Furthermore, when a verb is preceded by a preposition, in French the infinitive is always used, never the gerund. Be careful: in Spanish we say 'al llegar', but in French it is said 'en arrivant' to express simultaneity, although there is also 'après être arrivé' for anteriority, which has no direct equivalent in Spanish with a gerund.
rule: In French, the infinitive (infinitif) is used as a subject: 'Nager est bon pour la santé' (Swimming is good for health). It is also used as a direct object of verbs like 'aimer', 'vouloir', 'pouvoir' (without a preposition) or of verbs with a preposition: 'penser à faire' (to think about doing), 'commencer à faire' (to start doing), 'finir de faire' (to finish doing). The gérondif is formed with 'en + present participle' (in -ant) and expresses simultaneity, manner, cause, or condition: 'Il parle en mangeant' (He talks while eating), 'En étudiant, tu réussiras' (By studying, you will succeed). There is no gerund as a subject in French; the infinitive is always used. Additionally, the gérondif cannot be the object of a verb; for that, the infinitive is used. Exceptions: after prepositions like 'après', 'après + past infinitive' is used (after having done) and not the gérondif, because it indicates anteriority. With 'tout en + present participle', simultaneity is expressed with a nuance of concession: 'Tout en étant fatigué, il continue' (Even while being tired, he continues).

concept_examples.text: Nager est bon pour la santé.
concept_examples.translation: Swimming is good for health.
concept_examples.phonetic: /na.ʒe ɛ bɔ̃ puʁ la sɑ̃.te/

concept_examples.text: Elle pense à visiter Paris.
concept_examples.translation: She is thinking about visiting Paris.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɛl pɑ̃s a vi.zi.te pa.ʁi/

concept_examples.text: Il parle en mangeant.
concept_examples.translation: He talks while eating.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il paʁl ɑ̃ mɑ̃.ʒɑ̃/

concept_examples.text: Après avoir mangé, nous sortons.
concept_examples.translation: After having eaten, we go out.
concept_examples.phonetic: /a.pʁɛ.z‿a.vwaʁ mɑ̃.ʒe nu sɔʁ.tɔ̃/

common_error.explanation: In Spanish, 'pensar en' uses the preposition 'en', but in French the verb 'penser' is constructed with 'à' before an infinitive. This error occurs because the student directly transfers the Spanish preposition. It is important to learn the prepositions specific to each French verb.

examples.original: Voyager ouvre l'esprit.
examples.translation: Traveling opens the mind.
examples.note: In French, the infinitive can be a subject without a preposition, just like in Spanish. Note that the verb is conjugated in the third person singular.

examples.original: Apprendre le français est utile.
examples.translation: Learning French is useful.
examples.note: The infinitive as subject is followed by a conjugated verb. Unlike Spanish, 'el' is not used before the infinitive.

examples.original: Fumer est interdit ici.
examples.translation: Smoking is prohibited here.
examples.note: In French, one does not say 'el fumar' as in Spanish sometimes; simply the infinitive is used.

examples.original: Je veux acheter une voiture.
examples.translation: I want to buy a car.
examples.note: After verbs like 'vouloir' (to want), the infinitive is used without a preposition. 'de' is not used as in Spanish 'quiero comprar' (it is not 'quiero de comprar').

examples.original: Il commence à travailler.
examples.translation: He starts to work.
examples.note: The verb 'commencer' is constructed with the preposition 'à'. It is a common error to use 'de' by analogy with Spanish.

examples.original: Elle finit de manger.
examples.translation: She finishes eating.
examples.note: The verb 'finir' is constructed with 'de'. Note the contraction: 'de' + 'manger' does not contract, but if the following verb starts with a vowel, 'd'' is used (e.g., 'finir d'étudier').

levels.label: Le gérondif et l'infinitif après une préposition
levels.translation: The gerund and the infinitive after a preposition

examples.original: En marchant, je réfléchis.
examples.translation: While walking, I reflect.
examples.note: The gérondif is formed with 'en + present participle'. It indicates simultaneity with the main action.

examples.original: Il est parti en courant.
examples.translation: He left running.
examples.note: The gérondif expresses manner or way, similar to the Spanish gerund.

examples.original: Après avoir étudié, il sort.
examples.translation: After having studied, he goes out.
examples.note: To express anteriority, 'après + past infinitive' (avoir/être + past participle) is used. The gérondif is not used.

examples.original: Tout en travaillant, il écoute de la musique.
examples.phonetic: /tu.t‿ɑ̃ tʁa.va.jɑ̃ il e.kut də la my.zik/
examples.translation: Even while working, he listens to music.
examples.note: 'Tout en + gérondif' adds a nuance of concession or opposition.

translations.en: Gerunds and infinitives as subject and object

title: Les modales pour la déduction : devoir, pouvoir, être possible que / Modals for deduction: deber, poder, ser posible que
bridge: In Spanish, to deduce we use 'debe de ser', 'puede ser', 'podría ser', often with the subjunctive ('es posible que sea'). In French, the constructions are more direct: we use 'devoir' (must) for certainty, 'pouvoir' (can) for possibility, and the impersonal 'il est possible que' with the subjunctive. Important: in French, after 'devoir' and 'pouvoir' we use the infinitive, not the subjunctive, and to talk about past actions we use the compound form of the infinitive (avoir/être + past participle). Also, 'devoir' is not confused with 'deber de': in French the translation of 'debe de' is simply 'doit', without a preposition.
rule: To express deduction in French (B1 level), we mainly use: 1) 'devoir' + infinitive for strong probability (must): 'Il doit être malade' (He must be sick). In the past, 'devoir' + past infinitive (avoir/être + past participle): 'Il a dû être malade' (He must have been sick). 2) 'pouvoir' + infinitive for possibility (may, might): 'Il peut être malade' (He may be sick). In the past: 'Il a pu être malade' (He may have been sick). 3) The impersonal construction 'il est possible que' + subjunctive for more doubtful possibility: 'Il est possible qu'il soit malade' (It is possible that he is sick). Adverbs like 'peut-être' (maybe) are also used with affected inversion, but it is more formal: 'Peut-être est-il malade'. To deduce ongoing actions, 'devoir' + present infinitive is used: 'Il doit être en train de travailler'. In colloquial French, 'c'est possible que' with the subjunctive is used although the norm is 'il est possible que'. We do not use 'deber de' as in Spanish; 'devoir' does not take a preposition. The subjunctive is only used in constructions with 'que'.

concept_examples.text: Il doit être fatigué après ce voyage.
concept_examples.translation: He must be tired after this trip.
concept_examples.phonetic: il dwa ɛtʁ fatiɡe apʁə sə vwajaʒ

concept_examples.text: Elle peut avoir oublié nos rendez-vous.
concept_examples.translation: She may have forgotten our appointments.
concept_examples.phonetic: ɛl pø avwaʁ ublije no ʁɑ̃devu

concept_examples.text: Il est possible qu'il pleuve demain.
concept_examples.translation: It is possible that it will rain tomorrow.
concept_examples.phonetic: il ɛ pɔsibl kil plœv dəmɛ̃

concept_examples.text: Ils ont dû manquer leur train.
concept_examples.translation: They must have missed their train.
concept_examples.phonetic: ilz ɔ̃ dy mɑ̃ke lœʁ tʁɛ̃

common_error.wrong: Il doit être malade, car il n'est pas venu. (correct, but confusion: many use 'deber de' as 'doit de')
common_error.correct: Il doit être malade, car il n'est pas venu.
common_error.correct_alt: Il est possible qu'il soit malade, car il n'est pas venu.
common_error.explanation: The typical error is transferring the Spanish structure 'deber de + infinitive' by adding a preposition in French: 'doit de être' (incorrect). In French, 'devoir' is used directly with the infinitive. Additionally, some students confuse 'debe de' with moral 'deber': in French, the same verb 'devoir' is used for deduction, and also for obligation, but context clarifies it. To avoid the error, remember: do not use a preposition between the modal and the infinitive.

examples.original: Il doit être à la maison.
examples.phonetic: il dwa ɛtʁ a la mɛzɔ̃
examples.translation: He must be at home.
examples.note: Use of 'devoir' for strong probability, equivalent to 'debe de' in Spanish.

examples.original: Nous devons avoir le temps.
examples.translation: We must have time.
examples.note: Agreement of the modal with the subject; 'devoir' is conjugated in the present tense.

examples.original: Ils doivent être contents.
examples.translation: They must be happy.
examples.note: Notice the pronunciation of 'doivent' [dwav].

examples.original: Elle peut être en retard.
examples.translation: She may be late.
examples.note: 'Pouvoir' expresses possibility, similar to 'puede que' in Spanish.

examples.original: Ils peuvent avoir oublié.
examples.translation: They may have forgotten.
examples.note: Past infinitive for past actions: 'avoir oublié'.

examples.original: On pourrait être en retard à cause du trafic.
examples.phonetic: ɔ̃ puʁɛ ɛtʁ ɑ̃ ʁətaʁ a koz dy tʁafik
examples.translation: We could be late because of the traffic.
examples.note: The conditional 'pourrait' softens the possibility.

levels.label: L'hypothèse : il est possible que + subjonctif
levels.translation: Hypothesis: it is possible that + subjunctive

examples.original: Il est possible qu'il vienne.
examples.translation: It is possible that he comes.
examples.note: Subjunctive after 'il est possible que'.

examples.original: Il est possible qu'ils aient eu un problème.
examples.phonetic: il ɛ pɔsibl kilz‿ɛt‿y œ̃ pʁɔblɛm
examples.translation: It is possible that they had a problem.
examples.note: Past subjunctive: 'aient eu'.

examples.original: C'est possible qu'il soit malade.
examples.translation: It is possible that he is sick.
examples.note: In colloquial French, 'c'est possible que' is used although the norm is 'il est possible que'.
